guard_streams.source: Ofcom telecoms and pay-TV complaints Q1 2026 report

facts.detail: The current complaint release covers January to March 2026.
Complaints to Ofcom decreased compared with October to December 2025.
Fixed-broadband and pay-monthly-mobile complaint rates decreased quarter on quarter.
Landline and pay-TV complaint rates stayed at the previous-quarter level.

guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint trends are service-level indicators, not parcel network evidence.

facts.detail: Major-provider broadband complaints reached six per 100,000 customers in Q1 2026.
Ofcom described that broadband complaint level as the lowest on record.
The update compares the Q1 2026 level with a 2011 peak of 40 per 100,000 customers.
The figures concern complaints received by Ofcom about major providers, not all provider contacts.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint-rate improvements cannot establish address availability, technology or speed.

facts.detail: TalkTalk generated the highest fixed-broadband complaint rate in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints.
TalkTalk complaints mainly concerned faults, service and provisioning, complaint handling, and billing, pricing or charges.
Ofcom presents provider complaint rates for comparison with other measures such as price, availability and quality.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider complaint rankings are not a proxy for exact parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: Plusnet and TalkTalk were the most complained-about landline providers in Q1 2026.
Both recorded an increase compared with Q4 2025.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone generated the fewest landline complaints.
Rankings use complaints per 100,000 customers rather than raw complaint totals.

guard_streams.write_limit: Landline complaint performance cannot populate parcel broadband fields.

facts.detail: Sky Mobile generated the highest pay-monthly-mobile complaint rate.
Sky Mobile complaints mainly concerned experiences changing provider.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest mobile complaints.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers, while Sky and TalkTalk were the least complained-about.

guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile and pay-TV complaint rankings do not prove fixed-network parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom telecoms and pay-TV complaints Q1 2026 report

facts.detail: Ofcom normalises provider complaints per 100,000 customers.
The quarterly comparison covers major providers meeting the report's market-share threshold.
Ofcom states that it cannot act on individual consumer complaints.
Complaint data can help Ofcom identify possible systemic issues for further scrutiny.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regulatory complaint methodology cannot be converted into parcel availability or performance.

facts.detail: The previous unresolved-complaint threshold for ADR access was eight weeks.
Ofcom reduced the threshold to six weeks.
The six-week rule took effect on 8 April 2026.
Communications Ombudsman and CISAS were re-approved as telecoms ADR schemes.

guard_streams.write_limit: Dispute-resolution rights are customer-remedy evidence, not parcel network evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom reported that 79% of complaints received by the largest companies were resolved in under one week during the reviewed period.
Ninety-four percent were resolved within six weeks.
Around 700,000 consumers had a complaint still open at six weeks.
Only about 19% of that group obtained resolution or ADR referral before the former eight-week threshold.

guard_streams.write_limit: Aggregated complaint-resolution statistics cannot establish service availability at an address.

facts.detail: EE resubmitted information to Ofcom in April 2026.
The resubmission followed a discrepancy in EE broadband and landline fault data for 2024.
Specified EE fault data and associated industry averages remain subject to restatement.
Ofcom said it expected to reissue the 2025 customer-service report after reviewing the submission.

guard_streams.write_limit: Restated provider service data must not be treated as exact parcel performance.

facts.detail: The Northern Ireland Executive is the contracting authority.
Fibrus was awarded the Northern Ireland Project Gigabit contract.
The contract targets more than 9,000 premises across Northern Ireland.
The BDUK contract page was published on 16 December 2025.

guard_streams.write_limit: A regional award does not prove live service for any individual premise.

facts.detail: The Scottish Government is the contracting authority for the regional contract.
GoFibre was awarded the North East Scotland contract.
The contract targets around 63,000 premises.
The BDUK page was published on 15 July 2025.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional procurement scope cannot populate exact parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Gigaclear is the supplier for East Gloucestershire.
The contract value is £16 million.
The award targets around 4,400 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in February 2024 and requires detailed planning and construction before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract award and planned build do not establish current parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Yorkshire and parts of North Yorkshire contract

facts.detail: Quickline is the contracted supplier.
The contract value is £60 million.
The award targets around 28,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in February 2024 and the premises list remains subject to detailed-planning or technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional target totals cannot be promoted to exact current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North East Staffordshire, North Dorset, June and July 2026 contract progress

facts.detail: North East Staffordshire was awarded to Connect Fibre for £16.5 million and around 6,000 premises.
North Dorset was awarded to Wessex Internet for £6 million and more than 7,000 premises.
Rounded management snapshots show North East Staffordshire built counts moving from 2,410 in June to 2,860 in July, and West/parts North Yorkshire from 17,050 to 18,200.
The rounded total built count moved from 271,460 in June to 287,510 in July 2026.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded month-to-month management snapshots are lagged, non-parcel evidence and cannot assess exact delivery.
